title: Somehow we’re on Day SIX + SEVEN of TIFF!!!! 🥹 I’m so sad this journe...
transcript: I was having so much fun at TIFF that I simply decided I wasn't going to leave. Unfortunately, though, I don't have unlimited PTO. So while TIFF continued, I had to go back to work, which means you're getting two days of TIFF chaos into one vlog. Day 6, I had to check out of the hotel, which was sad because I loved this place. Luckily, my friend Michael very kindly volunteered to house me. We set up my little Toronto office in his house, spent a full day working, and as soon as I clocked out, hop back on the train downtown for the premiere of LA Bola Negra. Going into this, I knew there was some sort of theater connection, but I hadn't really looked it up. But this movie was actually all about theater. It was partially inspired by Federico Garcia Lorca, a queer playwright who was assassinated while writing a queer play in the 1930s. The play was called LA Bola Negra, and only four pages have ever been found. They take that story, they combine it with another play called LA Piedra Oscura, and then they added in a third modern storyline, and it creates this super epic Spanish queer film that I fell completely in love with, as did the entire audience, because there literally was a standing ovation for, like, 10 minutes. The performances are stunning, including Penelope Cruz, who has a relatively small but pivotal role where she sings and she dances. And I want her on stage immediately. Anyway, I cried a lot and I'm just thrilled I got to be there. And then suddenly it was day seven. I had to work again. But it was more fun because my friend Lynn came to visit and she brought her daughter, who I've never met. And I was just so happy. After work, I headed back downtown because TikTok had one more surreal opportunity for me. I got to interview Kat Sandler, the playright and go runner of Yaga. I have been so excited for the show and I am such a huge fan of cats. And I was so nervous. But then Kat and I just start talking about theater and Canadian content and obviously Hudson Williams, and we just clicked. It was the best. I am deeply obsessed with her. I can't wait for you to see this. I think you're gonna love the conversation. The day just kept getting better cause I got to meet Nova, my friend Sarah's dog. Sarah actually drove me to pick up my puppy. So getting to meet hers was so, so special. Literally the cutest dog. But I couldn't stay too long cause it was time for my last film of TIFF. I was kind of devastated, but luckily it was a really good one. The Liberation. This is a movie about Carrie Coon joining a cult. But what makes it even more interesting is it's actually based on the director's own Grandmother, I've always been fascinated by cults, and I thought this one was just so well done. Lily James plays the leader of the cult, and I now understand how people end up in a cult because she's so magnetic in this. But honestly, the whole cast is just. And Carrie Coon is just everything, obviously. And with that, my TIFF movie journey is now over. But we still have one more day. And it's all about Yaga and Hudson Williams. What an absolute dream.
